title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, as far as it can be inferred from this page and the previous one. Grothendieck has built flat group schemes over Z: the extended group \tilde S M_{ρ,σ} of relative dimension 10, the group S M_{ρ,σ} of relative dimension 7, and their quotients by a G_m (i(L_0)), of dimensions 9 and 6. They are assembled from pieces: tori T_0 and T_ρ, a group N'_σ, a Borel-type B'_0, G (presumably GL_2) and SG (presumably SL_2). By (44) these quotients split as semi-direct products SG^*_{ρ,σ}(0)·SG and G^*_{ρ,σ}(0)·G.

On this page he goes back to the 'unlimited' (profinite) situation of the equation of loops, for genus 0 with three points. The objects are as follows.
- \hat π_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on two generators.
- M_{0,3}^{!~} is a group of automorphisms of \hat π_{0,3} that preserve each inertia class and include the inner automorphisms. Presumably it is the group cut out by his 'équation des lacets', a GT-type group.
- M_{0,3}^{!~}(0) = Norm(L_0) is the subgroup of 'normalized' automorphisms, those normalizing the inertia subgroup L_0 at 0. This is the analogue of the Drinfeld–Ihara normal form σ(x)=x^λ, σ(y)=f^{-1}y^λ f.

The claim (45) is that there is a canonical homomorphism
 M_{0,3}^{!~} → M_{ρ,σ}(\hat Z)/Σ ≅ (T_0 × T_ρ(\hat Z) × T_σ(\hat Z))·SL(2,\hat Z) / Σ.
Here T_0 acts on SL(2,\hat Z) by conjugation, presumably the action of diag(λ,1), which is what makes the determinant equal to a cyclotomic-type character. Σ ≅ {±1}^3 is the product of the ±1's in T_ρ(\hat Z), T_σ(\hat Z) and SL(2,\hat Z).

The homomorphism is built in two pieces, glued by the decomposition (47) M^{!~} = M^{!~}(0)·\hat π_{0,3}:
- Piece (46): normalized automorphisms are sent to SG^*_{ρ,σ}(0)(\hat Z)/Σ_0 ⊂ SG^*_{ρ,σ}(\hat Z)/Σ_0.
- Inner automorphisms: these go through the composite \hat π_{0,3} ↪ \hat G^+_{0,3} → SL(2,\hat Z)'.
  - \hat G^+_{0,3} is identified with the profinite completion of SL(2,Z)' (or of PSL(2,Z)). It contains \hat π_{0,3} as the completion of Γ(2)/±1, which has index 6.
  - SL(2,\hat Z)' is the congruence completion.

The next page extends the map to the full M_{0,3}^~, in which M^{!~} is normal of index 6 (quotient S_3, the permutations of the three points), via M_{0,3}^~ = M^{!~}(0)·S^+_{0,3}.

Interpretation: this is a combinatorial or 'anabelian' linearization of the GT-type group. It is the analogue, for the abstract automorphism group, of the Galois representation on the Tate module of the Legendre family y^2 = x(x-1)(x-λ), whose monodromy is Γ(2). The three ±1 ambiguities correspond to the quadratic-twist and sign ambiguities. It serves the larger aim of the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets': testing and realizing the loop-equation group through linear (GL_2/SL_2-type) algebraic envelopes.
errors: No outright error is visible, but there is a gap. Defining (45) requires that elements of M_{0,3}^{!~}(0) preserve the congruence kernel of \hat π_{0,3} → SL(2,\hat Z). Equivalently, the induced action must descend to the congruence completion. For Galois elements this follows from the Legendre family. For an abstractly defined loop-equation group it needs proof (presumably given in §VIII / §46 on earlier pages); it is not shown on this page.
The precise meaning of the primes (SL(2,\hat Z)', SL(2,Z)'^) and of Σ_0 versus Σ is ambiguous on this page; the index-6 claim fits Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z).

ideas.what: Decomposition of the pure inertia-preserving automorphism group of \hat F_2 as normalized automorphisms times inner automorphisms, M^{!~} = Norm(L_0)·\hat π_{0,3}
ideas.modern_name: normalized (Drinfeld–Ihara) form of GT elements; Out vs Aut of \hat F_2

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphism from the (loop-equation / GT-type) automorphism group of \hat π_{0,3} to a profinite linear group (T_0×T_ρ×T_σ)·SL(2,\hat Z) modulo {±1}^3, built via the congruence quotient \hat π_{0,3} → Γ(2)^ → SL(2,\hat Z)
ideas.modern_name: linearization of GT on the congruence (Legendre/Γ(2)) quotient; abstract analogue of the Galois representation on the Tate module of the Legendre curve
ideas.usually_credited_to: partially Ihara (Galois representations arising from F_2), work on GT and congruence subgroups (Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps, Boggi); unsure of an exact match

ideas.what: Identification of the orbifold group \hat G^+_{0,3} with the completion of (P)SL(2,Z)', containing \hat π_{0,3} as the index-6 completion of Γ(2)/±1, with quotient S_3 = permutations of {0,1,∞}
ideas.modern_name: π_1^orb of M_{1,1} / λ-line as Γ(2)\H
ideas.where_published: related remarks in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower in low dimension)

ideas.what: Extension of the pure homomorphism to the full M_{0,3}^~ via the S_3 of permutations of the three points (next page)

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs a canonical 'linear envelope' homomorphism from his loop-equation automorphism group of \hat π_{0,3} into M_{ρ,σ}(\hat Z)/Σ. This is a GL_2/SL_2-type profinite group built from flat group schemes over Z of dimensions 6–10. Its image, its kernel, and its relation to the congruence subgroup problem are not analysed here.
missed.quote: on trouve par passage au quotient via (17) un homomorphisme canonique (45) M_{0,3}^{!~} → M_{ρ,σ}(\hat Z)/Σ
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT (or GT-type groups) act compatibly on the congruence completion of Γ(2) is a live question, connected to Boggi's work and congruence-subgroup questions for M_{g,n}. An explicit algebraic-group target over Z with a precise {±1}^3 ambiguity would be a concrete test object; I am not aware of this group-scheme formulation in the literature.

missed.claim: This is implicitly a bridge between the combinatorial GT-type group and the Galois representation of the Legendre elliptic family (Γ(2), with determinant given by T_0). The 'linearization' of anabelian automorphism groups through modular (SL_2) quotients is formulated as a morphism of group schemes over Z.
missed.quote: T_0 × T_ρ(\hat Z) × T_σ(\hat Z) . SL(2,\hat Z) ... opérant sur SL(2,\hat Z) via le facteur T_0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is relevant to comparing GT with motivic/elliptic Galois images, for instance in elliptic GT (Enriquez) and in Nakamura's and Hain–Matsumoto's work on the Galois action on the Γ(2) / elliptic tower.

deep.surprise_reason: This is an unpublished, fairly explicit construction: a canonical homomorphism from Grothendieck's loop-equation automorphism group to a profinite linear group built from Z-group schemes, modulo {±1}^3. The underlying idea, Galois/GT acting through the Legendre/Γ(2) congruence quotient, is known in spirit, so the novelty lies mainly in the formalism and the unchecked descent to the congruence completion.
transcription_corrections: Marginal note reads 'compte tenu de (13)' and the superscript insertion 'par passage au quotient via (17)'.
Page number at top is 498 (archive page 393).
'et du compris' is more likely 'et du composé' (the composite \hat π_{0,3} ↪ \hat G^+_{0,3} → SL(2,\hat Z)').
Below \hat G^+_{0,3} the symbol is '≀' (isomorphism), i.e. \hat G^+_{0,3} ≃ SL(2,Z)'^, not '∪'.
The first target in (46) is SG^*_{ρ,σ}(0)(\hat Z)/Σ_0, mapping into SG^*_{ρ,σ}(\hat Z)/Σ_0.

In (45), a struck-out initial symbol precedes T_0 (with a small 0 subscript), so the target reads T_0 × T_ρ(\hat Z) × T_σ(\hat Z)·SL(2,\hat Z); the brace with '^' denotes this description of M_{ρ,σ}(\hat Z).
